arxiv-1904-00518.title: A Comparative Study of Asynchronous Many-Tasking Runtimes: Cilk, Charm++, ParalleX and AM++
arxiv-1904-00518.creator: Abhishek Kulkarni, Andrew Lumsdaine
arxiv-1904-00518.description: Abstract We evaluate and compare four contemporary and emerging runtimes for high-performance computing (HPC) applications: Cilk, Charm ++ , ParalleX and AM ++ . We compare along three bases: programming model, execution model and the implementation on an underlying machine model.

arxiv-2102-05385.creator: Shreya Tayade 1 , Peter Rost 2 and Andreas Maeder 2
arxiv-2102-05385.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a cloud based Automated Guided vehicle (AGV) control system. A controller in an Edge cloud sends the control inputs to an AGV to follow a predefined reference track over a wireless channel. The AGV feedback the position update via uplink channel.

arxiv-2209-14057.creator: Umamaheswara Sharma B, Ravichandra Sadam
arxiv-2209-14057.description: Abstract Context: Cross-project defect prediction (CPDP) models are being developed to optimize the testing resources. Objectives: Proposing an ensemble classification framework for CPDP as many existing models are lacking with better performances and analysing the main objectives of CPDP from the outcomes of the proposed classification framework.

arxiv-2210-10499.title: Extensions of two-field mimetic gravity
arxiv-2210-10499.creator: Yunlong Zheng, and Haomin Rao
arxiv-2210-10499.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yunlong Zheng, and Haomin Rao. Two-field mimetic gravity was recently realized by looking at the singular limit of the conformal transformation between the auxiliary metric and the physical metric with two scalar fields involved. In this paper, we reanalyze the singular conformal limit and find a more general solution for the conformal factor A A , which greatly broadens the form of two-field mimetic constraint and thus extends the two-field mimetic gravity.

arxiv-2212-11072.title: Global existence and Blow-up for the 1D damped compressible Euler equations with time and space dependent perturbation
arxiv-2212-11072.creator: Yuusuke Sugiyama
arxiv-2212-11072.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuusuke Sugiyama. In this paper, we consider the 1D Euler equation with time and space dependent damping term − a ⁡ ( t , x ) ​ v -a(t,x)v . It has long been known that when a ⁡ ( t , x ) a(t,x) is a positive constant or 0 0 , the solution exists globally in time or blows up in finite time, respectively. We prove that those results are invariant with respect to time and space dependent perturbations.

arxiv-2407-02278.description: Abstract We report on the realization and characterization of a novel magic-wavelength nanofiber-based two-color optical dipole trap for cesium that allows us to generate two diametral periodic one-dimensional arrays of trapping sites with a spacing significantly smaller than half the resonant free-space wavelength of the cesium D2-transition.

arxiv-2411-09450.creator: Aida Abiad, Jiang Zhou
arxiv-2411-09450.description: Abstract For a graph G G , its k k -th power G k G^{k} is constructed by placing an edge between two vertices if they are within distance k k of each other. The k k -independence number α k ​ ( G ) \alpha_{k}(G) is defined as the independence number of G k G^{k} .

arxiv-2507-06086.title: QuHE: Optimizing Utility-Cost in Quantum Key Distribution and Homomorphic Encryption Enabled Secure Edge Computing Networks
arxiv-2507-06086.creator: Liangxin Qian, Yang Li, and Jun Zhao
arxiv-2507-06086.description: Abstract Ensuring secure and efficient data processing in mobile edge computing (MEC) systems is a critical challenge. While quantum key distribution (QKD) offers unconditionally secure key exchange and homomorphic encryption (HE) enables privacy-preserving data processing, existing research fails to address the comprehensive trade-offs among QKD utility, HE security, and system costs.

pmc-10784717.title: Ponatinib Improved the Prognosis of Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Japanese Single-Center Cohort Study
pmc-10784717.creator: Nagi Tozawa, Takaya Yamashita, Miho Nara, Yuki Fujioka, Sho Ikeda, Takahiro Kobayashi, Isuzu Kobayashi, Akihiro Kitadate, Yoshihiro Kameoka, Naoto Takahashi

In recent years, there has been increased interest in the possibility of long-term survival without allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) or maintenance therapy.

pmc-12525330.title: CRISPR-Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Mammarenavirus machupoense Virus: Optimization and Evaluation of Multiplex Capability
pmc-12525330.creator: Marina A. Kapitonova, Anna V. Shabalina, Vladimir G. Dedkov, Anna S. Dolgova
pmc-12525330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) is a zoonotic disease caused by Mammarenavirus machupoense (MACV) featuring severe neurological and hemorrhagic symptoms and a high mortality rate. BHF is usually diagnosed by serological tests or real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR); these methods are often inaccessible in endemic regions due to a lack of laboratory infrastructure, creating a demand for sensitive and rapid equipment-free alternatives.

pmc-12593528.title: Low Income Has a Negative Effect on Survival Following Diagnosis of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer—A Population‐Based Cohort Study
pmc-12593528.creator: Malin Ljunggren, Caroline E Dietrich, Cecilia Merk, Gabriella Palmer, Anna Martling, Caroline Nordenvall
pmc-12593528.description: BackgroundTreatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) has seen great advances but may not be equally available for all patients.AimTo evaluate the impact of socioeconomic status on cancer‐specific survival after diagnosis of mCRC, with emphasis on potential temporal trends in the effect of income.

pmc-13082942.title: Diagnostic value of calcitonin for lateral cervical lymph node metastasis in medullary thyroid carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13082942.creator: Li Zhang, Shuangyan Wang, Xun Ye, Xinbin Lin
pmc-13082942.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic performance of preoperative serum calcitonin (Ctn) in detecting lateral cervical lymph node metastasis (LLNM) in patients with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), identify the optimal threshold, and provide evidence for individualized neck dissection strategies.MethodsRelevant Chinese and English databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang, and VIP, were systematically searched.

pmc-13179330.title: The role of fear learning in the development of psychosis: an EEG study utilizing a differential fear conditioning paradigm in people with psychotic vulnerability
pmc-13179330.creator: Metin Özyagcilar, Nilay Esin Ahrens-Demirdal, Anja Riesel, Tina B Lonsdorf, Tania M Lincoln
pmc-13179330.description: By studying how individuals in an “at-risk” state of psychosis learn about threat and safety cues – specifically, how they develop and unlearn fear responses to neutral cues – we might better understand the mechanisms leading to heightened arousal and fear that are characteristic of acute psychotic episodes.

pmc-13259496.title: Plant Functional Traits and Diversity of Community Link to the Plant Invasion Dominance in the Subalpine Wetland of Shennongjia National Nature Reserve, China
pmc-13259496.creator: Ruifeng Zhang, Hengyu Xiong, Yuanyuan Liu, Yuhan Xu, Ligai Huang, Bingnan Wen, Wenchao Zhao, Ping Zhao, Binyuan Xu, Yanfeng Bai, Ran Meng
pmc-13259496.description: Plant invasions pose a significant threat to plant community integrity at high latitudes and altitudes, particularly under the backdrop of ongoing climate change and anthropogenic disturbance. However, how plant invasion and increasing invasion intensity reshape community functional traits and multidimensional diversity in high-altitude wetland ecosystems remain poorly understood.

pmc-13312216.title: Preventing parastomal hernia following radical cystectomy with ileal conduit diversion: outcomes of prophylactic mesh reinforcement
pmc-13312216.creator: Pavel Navratil, Minh Nguyet Tranova, Oleg Izmaylov, Jiri Chalupnik, Katerina Balasova, Miroslav Louda
pmc-13312216.description: IntroductionParastomal hernia (PH) is a frequent long-term complication following radical cystectomy with ileal conduit urinary diversion. Evidence supporting preventive strategies in urologic surgery remains limited. This study evaluated the impact of prophylactic mesh reinforcement during ileal conduit formation on PH incidence and postoperative outcomes.

pmc-13397747.title: Prognostic impact of platelet count trajectories in acute decompensated heart failure: a retrospective cohort analysis
pmc-13397747.creator: Gil Marcus, Maya Barzilay, Shiri L. Maymon, Eran Kalmanovich, Gil Moravsky, Ido Minha, Avishay Grupper, Shmuel Fuchs, Sa’ar Minha
pmc-13397747.description: AimsTo determine whether in-hospital platelet count trajectories during admission for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) are associated with early and longer-term outcomes after discharge.MethodsWe performed a single-centre retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized for ADHF (2007–2017). After excluding in-hospital deaths and cases without paired platelet measurements, 6,789 patients were analyzed from an initial 8,332.

pmc-13438011.title: Human dissection and comparative anatomy: Archaeological evidence for nineteenth‐century anatomical practice at University College London
pmc-13438011.creator: Wendy Birch, Tania Kausmally
pmc-13438011.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The history of anatomical dissection in nineteenth‐century Britain has largely been reconstructed from archival sources, including legislation, institutional records and medical writings. Archaeological evidence for the material practices of anatomy schools, however, remains comparatively limited. In 2010, redevelopment within the main quadrangle of University College London (UCL) revealed a substantial assemblage of human and animal skeletal remains associated with the institution's early anatomy school.

pmc-13557396.title: Brain structural and functional connectivity converge prenatally but diverge after birth
pmc-13557396.creator: Ruoke Zhao, Mingyang Li, Yuqi Zhang, Ruike Chen, Chenglin Ning, Zhiyong Zhao, Zhihan Yan, Meihao Wang, Dan Wu
pmc-13557396.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Brain anatomical architecture supports its functional activity and complex cognitive processes. However, how the structure–function (SF) relationship establishes and develops during early life, as well as its underlying mechanisms, remain largely unclear. To address these questions, we leveraged multimodal MRI data from two large-scale public databases, the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) and the Baby Connectome Project (BCP), to characterize the spatiotemporal dynamics of SF coupling from the perinatal period to toddlerhood.

pmc-13657472.title: Exploring the potential of mRNA vaccines in combatting communicable and non-communicable diseases in low-income and lower-middle-income countries
pmc-13657472.creator: Faida Paison, Queen Ntumurize, Gustave Munyurangabo, Sifa Nayihiki, Yue Jingze, Secret Atukunda, Rosine Ikuzwe Shabe, Janvier Habumugisha, Fortunate Ayebare, Fabrice Kayitare, Betty Amikoro, Willy Mazimpaka, Jean de Dieu Niyoyita, Biyun Su
pmc-13657472.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The global health landscape is increasingly dominated by a double burden of communicable diseases (CDs) and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), with low-income and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs) being disproportionately affected due to geographic, demographic, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. While infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and diarrheal illnesses continue to cause high mortality rates, particularly in LMICs, NCDs such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, and chronic pulmonary conditions are rising rapidly due to demographic shifts and lifestyle changes.
